If you're like me, you've probably spent way too much time falling down the Wikipedia rabbit hole via random articles. Now the official app has finally rolled out a way to do exactly that — well, a widget, to be precise.

There's finally a button that takes you straight to a random Wikipedia article

Today's Wikipedia iOS app update brings a fun and rather useful new addition: a "Random Article" widget you can place on your iPhone and iPad home screens.

It comes in two sizes (large and medium), and even has a cute mascot to keep you company.

Tap the widget and you'll be taken straight to a completely random Wikipedia article, with "Random Mode" enabled to boot.

No need to leave the app and tap the widget again. Just hit the "Random Article" button and it'll keep rolling the dice, sending you deeper and deeper down that random rabbit hole.

Have fun, but mind that time doesn't quietly slip away! Earlier this summer, the Wikipedia app already added a history-trivia mini-game.

You'll find this brand-new widget in today's update of the Wikipedia iPhone and iPad app.
